config.title: Image Gallery

intro.title: Image Gallery
intro.body: In this lesson, you will build a simple image gallery component that displays a collection of pictures. You will learn how to use Angular's structural directives, specifically *ngFor, to loop through an array of image data and render it dynamically in the template. The main technologies involved are Angular components, TypeScript arrays, and HTML for structure and styling. By the end, you'll have a functional gallery that you can customize with your own images.
intro.usecase: Image galleries are fundamental UI components found across modern web applications. In e-commerce platforms like Amazon or Etsy, product galleries allow users to browse multiple photos of items with navigation controls. Social media apps like Instagram and Facebook use sophisticated galleries to display user photo collections with interactive features. Media websites and portfolio platforms rely on galleries to showcase visual content in organized, navigable layouts. As a developer, you'll frequently implement galleries for product displays, photo albums, media libraries, and content carousels.

objectives: Implement a component to display a collection of images
Configure an array to store image data with properties like URL and title
Bind image data to template elements using Angular directives
Control image display with conditional rendering based on state
Integrate event handlers to navigate between gallery images
Manipulate component state to track the current image index
Initialize a gallery with default images and navigation controls
Render a responsive image gallery with interactive features

steps.title: Import Component and CommonModule from Angular core
steps.instruction: Import Component from '@angular/core' and CommonModule from '@angular/common' in your TypeScript file.
steps.hint: Use the import statement to bring in Angular's core decorator and common directives module.
steps.expectedOutcome: Your code will have the necessary Angular imports to create a component and use common directives.
successCriteria: Component and CommonModule are imported from their respective Angular packages.
steps.feedbackCorrect: Nice! Proceed to the next step.
steps.feedbackPartial: You're close. Make sure you're importing both Component and CommonModule from their correct packages.
steps.feedbackWrong: The imports are missing or incorrect. Check that you're importing Component from '@angular/core' and CommonModule from '@angular/common'.

steps.title: Initialize the image data array
steps.instruction: Inside the ImageGalleryComponent class, create an images property as an array of objects with id, src, alt, and title properties. Initialize it with at least two sample image objects.
steps.hint: Define a property in the class using TypeScript syntax: images = [ { id: 1, src: '...', alt: '...', title: '...' }, ... ];
steps.expectedOutcome: The component will have a typed images array containing sample image data.
successCriteria: The ImageGalleryComponent class contains an images property initialized as an array of objects with id, src, alt, and title properties.
steps.feedbackCorrect: Nice! Proceed to the next step.
steps.feedbackPartial: You've added an images property, but check that it includes all required properties (id, src, alt, title) and is properly initialized.
steps.feedbackWrong: The images property is missing or doesn't match the required structure. Review the instruction and try again.

steps.title: Define the selectedImage state property
steps.instruction: Add a selectedImage property to the ImageGalleryComponent class to track the currently selected image. Initialize it as null.
steps.hint: Declare a property with type 'any' or a specific image interface, and set its initial value to null.
steps.expectedOutcome: The component will have a selectedImage property initialized to null, ready to store the currently selected image.
successCriteria: The ImageGalleryComponent class has a selectedImage property declared and initialized to null.
steps.feedbackCorrect: Nice! Proceed to the next step.
steps.feedbackPartial: You've added a property, but make sure it's named 'selectedImage' and initialized to null.
steps.feedbackWrong: The selectedImage property is missing or incorrectly defined. Add a property named selectedImage initialized to null.

steps.title: Create the selectImage handler method
steps.instruction: Inside the ImageGalleryComponent class, define a method named selectImage that takes an image object as a parameter and sets the selectedImage property to that image.
steps.hint: The method should have a parameter (like 'image') and assign it to this.selectedImage.
steps.expectedOutcome: The component now has a selectImage method that will update the selected image when called.
successCriteria: The selectImage method is defined in the component class with a parameter and sets this.selectedImage.
steps.feedbackCorrect: Nice! Proceed to the next step.
steps.feedbackPartial: You're close! Make sure your selectImage method has a parameter and assigns it to this.selectedImage.
steps.feedbackWrong: The selectImage method isn't defined correctly. It should take an image parameter and set this.selectedImage to that image.

steps.title: Add the main container div to the template
steps.instruction: In the component's template, add a div element with the class 'gallery' to serve as the main container for your image gallery.
steps.hint: Add the div element inside the template string. Use double quotes for the class attribute.
steps.expectedOutcome: The component template now contains a div element with class 'gallery' as the main container.
successCriteria: The template includes a div element with class attribute set to 'gallery'.
steps.feedbackCorrect: Nice! Proceed to the next step.
steps.feedbackPartial: You're close. Make sure you've added a div element with the class 'gallery' in the template string.
steps.feedbackWrong: The template doesn't contain the required div element. Add a div with class 'gallery' to the template.

steps.title: Display the selected image section
steps.instruction:
Inside the component's template, add a
element that conditionally renders when selectedImage is truthy using *ngIf. Inside this div, add an element with its src bound to selectedImage.url and alt text bound to selectedImage.title.
steps.hint: Use *ngIf="selectedImage" on a div to show the section only when an image is selected. Use property binding [src] and [alt] on the img tag.
steps.expectedOutcome: The template will include a conditional section that displays the selected image with proper binding.
successCriteria: A div with *ngIf="selectedImage" is added to the template, containing an img element with [src] and [alt] bound to selectedImage properties.
steps.feedbackCorrect: Nice! Proceed to the next step.
steps.feedbackPartial: You've added some of the required elements. Make sure you have both the *ngIf directive on a div and an img element with property bindings for src and alt.
steps.feedbackWrong: The template doesn't yet include the conditional selected image section. Add a div with *ngIf and an img element with property bindings.

steps.title: Create the thumbnail grid with *ngFor
steps.instruction: Add a div element to your component's template that uses *ngFor to iterate through the images array and display each image's title as text content.
steps.hint: Use *ngFor="let image of images" on a div element, then display {{ image.title }} inside the div.
steps.expectedOutcome: The template now contains a div with *ngFor that will generate a list of image titles when rendered.
successCriteria: A div element with *ngFor directive iterating over 'images' is added to the template, displaying each image's title.
steps.feedbackCorrect: Nice! Proceed to the next step.
steps.feedbackPartial: You've added a div, but make sure it includes the *ngFor directive with 'let image of images' and displays {{ image.title }} inside.
steps.feedbackWrong: The thumbnail grid with *ngFor was not correctly added. Check that you've added a div with *ngFor="let image of images" and {{ image.title }} inside.

steps.title: Wire click events to thumbnails
steps.instruction: Add (click) event binding to each thumbnail image in the *ngFor loop that calls the selectImage method with the current image object.
steps.hint: Use Angular's event binding syntax: (click)="selectImage(image)" on the img element inside the *ngFor loop.
steps.analogousExample:
// Similar: event binding in Angular template
<button (click)="handleClick(item)">Click me</button>
steps.expectedOutcome: Each thumbnail image should now have a click event that triggers the selectImage method with the corresponding image object.
successCriteria: The img element inside the *ngFor loop has (click)="selectImage(image)" event binding.
steps.feedbackCorrect: Nice! Proceed to the next step.
steps.feedbackPartial: You're close! Make sure you've added (click)="selectImage(image)" to the img element inside the *ngFor loop.
steps.feedbackWrong: The click event binding is missing or incorrect. Add (click)="selectImage(image)" to the thumbnail img element.

steps.title: Add active state styling to selected thumbnail
steps.instruction: Add an [ngClass] binding to the thumbnail div to apply an 'active' CSS class when the thumbnail's image matches the selectedImage.
steps.hint: Use [ngClass] with an object expression like {'active': image === selectedImage}. This will add the 'active' class conditionally.
steps.expectedOutcome: The thumbnail div now has an [ngClass] binding that conditionally applies the 'active' class based on whether the image matches the selectedImage.
successCriteria: The thumbnail div includes [ngClass] with an object expression that adds the 'active' class when image === selectedImage.
steps.feedbackCorrect: Nice! Proceed to the next step.
steps.feedbackPartial: You're on the right track, but check the [ngClass] binding syntax. It should be an object expression like {'active': image === selectedImage}.
steps.feedbackWrong: The thumbnail div doesn't have the correct [ngClass] binding. Review how to apply conditional CSS classes in Angular.
